message.content:
I'm investigating the Vue frontend project at `d:\_ntu台大\aiProject\_dev\_frontend\chatai` (an NTU chatbot app called "ntu-chatbot", Vue 3 + vue-router 4 + TypeScript + Vite + Tailwind + pnpm). This app serves multiple "flows" (flowId=6,7,8...) which are different AI chatbot assistants (e.g. flow 7 is "學習規劃探索助手" / learning-planning-exploration-assistant, flow 8 is "未來教室小助手" / classroom FAQ assistant). I need to understand its architecture deeply enough to plan integrating a SEPARATE, already-built Vue app (an immersive full-page multi-route experience with its own vue-router, its own global CSS reset including `body { overflow: hidden }`, its own fonts, its own design tokens) as the new frontend specifically for flow 7, WITHOUT affecting or breaking any other flow's UI (flow 6, flow 8, etc. must keep using the existing generic chat UI).

Please investigate and report back on:

1. **Routing structure**: Read `src/router` or equivalent (look for router.ts, router/index.ts, or similar) — what routes exist, how is a "flow" selected/identified in the URL (query param? path param? route meta?), and where does flow-specific logic branch.

2. **App entry & root structure**: Read `src/main.ts` and the root `App.vue` — how is the app mounted, is there a single global layout wrapping all flows, are there global styles applied at a level that would affect a nested app (e.g. global CSS resets, html/body styles, font loading)?

3. **Flow identification mechanism**: Find where `flowId` (or similar) is read/used — likely in `src/lib/constant.ts` (SIMPLE_MODE_FLOW_IDS was seen there), `src/hooks/ChatProvider.vue`, `src/hooks/useAICall.ts`, `src/components/MainPage.vue`. Explain concretely: given a URL like `?flow=7` or `/chat/7`, what Vue components/views end up rendering, and is there already a per-flow conditional rendering pattern (e.g. `v-if="flowId === 8"` for special UI like the classroom FAQ's image upload)?

4. **Build/deployment**: Read `package.json` scripts, `vite.config.ts` — is this a single SPA build deployed as one bundle? Is there any existing pattern of code-splitting or lazy-loading per-route/per-flow components? Check `predeploy`/`deploy` scripts (gh-pages mentioned) to understand hosting model (single static site, base path, etc).

5. **Existing "special flow" precedent**: Flow 8 apparently already has custom UI behavior (image attachment) different from other flows per `ChatProvider.vue` comments. Find and describe how that per-flow special-casing is currently implemented in the components/views layer (not just the provider) — is there a distinct Vue page/component for flow 8, or is it all one generic `MainPage.vue` with conditionals? This precedent matters a lot for deciding whether flow 7 should get its own dedicated route/mount point.

6. Also check if there's any existing iframe usage, micro-frontend pattern, or Web Component wrapping anywhere in this repo or `chatai_backend` static file serving (Program.cs `UseStaticFiles`) that could hint at how a separate build might already be intended to be served alongside this app.

Report concisely (structured by the 6 numbered points above) with concrete file paths and short code excerpts. I don't need you to propose the integration solution — just give me the accurate architectural facts so I can design the plan myself.

- figma:figma-code-connect: Creates and maintains Figma Code Connect template files that map Figma components to code snippets. Use when the user mentions Code Connect, Figma component mapping, design-to-code translation, or asks to create/update .figma.ts or .figma.js files.
- figma:figma-create-new-file: **MANDATORY prerequisite** — you MUST invoke this skill BEFORE every `create_new_file` tool call. NEVER call `create_new_file` directly without loading this skill first. Trigger whenever the user wants a new blank Figma file — a new design, FigJam, or Slides file — or when you need a fresh file before calling `use_figma`. Usage — /figma-create-new-file [editorType] [fileName] (e.g. /figma-create-new-file figjam My Whiteboard, /figma-create-new-file slides Q3 Review)
- figma:figma-design-to-code: **MANDATORY prerequisite** — you MUST invoke this skill BEFORE calling the `get_design_context` Figma MCP tool. You MUST trigger this skill whenever the user wants to implement, build, port, or code up a Figma design as code. Example prompts (not exhaustive) are 'implement this Figma design', 'build this screen from Figma', 'turn this Figma into code', 'design to code'. This skill provides critical instructions and steps to the agent on how to correctly implement Figma designs in code and must NOT be skipped.
- figma:figma-generate-design: Use this skill alongside figma-use when the task involves translating an application page, view, or multi-section layout into Figma. Triggers: 'write to Figma', 'create in Figma from code', 'push page to Figma', 'take this app/page and build it in Figma', 'create a screen', 'build a landing page in Figma', 'update the Figma screen to match code', 'convert this modal/dialog/drawer/panel to Figma'. This is the preferred workflow skill whenever the user wants to build or update a full page, modal, dialog, drawer, sidebar, panel, or any composed multi-section view in Figma from code or a description. Discovers design system components, variables, and styles from Code Connect files, existing screens, and library search, then imports them and assembles views incrementally section-by-section using design system tokens instead of hardcoded values.
- figma:figma-generate-diagram
- figma:figma-generate-library: Build or update a professional-grade design system in Figma from a codebase. Use when the user wants to create variables/tokens, build component libraries, create individual components with proper variant sets and variable bindings, set up theming (light/dark modes), document foundations, or reconcile gaps between code and Figma. Also use when the user asks to create or generate any component in Figma — even a single one — since components require proper variable foundations, variant states, and design token bindings to be production-quality. This skill teaches WHAT to build and in WHAT ORDER — it complements the `figma-use` skill which teaches HOW to call the Plugin API. Both skills should be loaded together.
- figma:figma-implement-motion
- figma:figma-swiftui
- figma:figma-use: **MANDATORY prerequisite** — you MUST invoke this skill BEFORE every `use_figma` tool call. NEVER call `use_figma` directly without loading this skill first. Skipping it causes common, hard-to-debug failures. Trigger whenever the user wants to perform a write action or a unique read action that requires JavaScript execution in the Figma file context — e.g. create/edit/delete nodes, set up variables or tokens, build components and variants, modify auto-layout or fills, bind variables to properties, or inspect file structure programmatically.
- figma:figma-use-figjam
- figma:figma-use-motion
- figma:figma-use-slides
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by running the app and observing behavior. Use when asked to verify a PR, confirm a fix works, test a change manually, check that a feature works, or validate local changes before pushing.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). Let me create a comprehensive report. ## Architecture Investigation Report: NTU Chatbot Frontend (ntu-chatbot) Based on my thorough analysis of the codebase, here are the architectural findings for the Vue 3 chatbot application: ### 1. **Routing Structure** **File**: `src/main.ts` (lines 27-48) The app uses a **query parameter-based flow identification pattern**, NOT path-based routing: - Routes defined: `/`, `/help`, `/docs`, `/login`, `/rating` (static page routes) - **Flow selection**: Via `?flow=X` query parameter (e.g., `/?flow=7`, `/?flow=8`) - **Route guard logic** (lines 40-48): - Unauthenticated users redirected to `/login` - Authenticated users on `/` without `?flow` parameter default to `flow=6` - Flow-specific branching happens **within** the same `/` route, not via separate routes All flows render to the **same single route** (`/`), meaning the generic chat UI wraps all flows. The flow parameter flows down to components via Vue Router's `route.query.flow`. ### 2. **App Entry & Root Structure** **Files**: `src/main.ts`, `src/App.vue`, `src/Providers.vue` **Mounting**: Standard Vue 3 SPA — mounts to `#app` div in `index.html` (single mount point). **Root component hierarchy**: ``` App.vue ├── Background (static gradient) ├── Providers (context setup) │ ├── TooltipProvider (UI library) │ ├── ChatProvider (state & flow logic) │ │ ├── Header │ │ └── RouterView (routes all flow into HomeView) │ └── HomeView (always renders) │ ├── ScrollArea │ │ └── MainPage (flow-conditional rendering) │ │ ├── Static welcome UI (bird images, title) │ │ ├── PromptBlock (conditionally hidden for flows 6,7,8) │ │ └── Messages (chat display, all flows share this) │ └── InputBlock (conditionally shows flow-specific inputs) ``` **Global CSS/Styles** applied in `src/assets/index.css`: - Line 124-129: Global `html, body { height: 100%; }` — full viewport height - CSS reset via Tailwind `@layer base` - Custom CSS variables (oklch colors) for theming - NO global `body { overflow: hidden }` or restrictive resets that would interfere with a nested app **Index.html** (`index.html` line 36): ```html
``` Single div with flex column layout. The app structure is a **vertical flex layout** consuming full viewport height. ### 3. **Flow Identification Mechanism** **Primary source**: `route.query.flow` from vue-router **Key files showing flow logic**: - **`src/lib/constant.ts`** (line 8): ```javascript export const SIMPLE_MODE_FLOW_IDS = ["3", "6", "7", "8"]; ``` These flows skip QA database search, go directly to AI. - **`src/components/MainPage.vue`** (lines 9-15): ```javascript const isSimpleMode = computed(() => route.query.flow === "3"); const isDirectChatMode = computed(() => ["6", "7", "8"].includes(route.query.flow as string), ); ``` Flows 6, 7, 8 hide the "快速找到承辦單位" (quick FAQ) prompt block. - **`src/components/InputBlock.vue`** (lines 124-125): ```vue ``` Flow-specific UI components conditionally rendered in input area. - **`src/hooks/ChatProvider.vue`** (lines 98-123): ```javascript watch( () => route.query.flow, (flow) => { if (flowValue === "7") { openingMessage = ADVISING_OPENING_MESSAGE; // Learning planning assistant } else if (flowValue === "8") { openingMessage = CLASSROOM_FAQ_OPENING_MESSAGE; // Classroom FAQ } }, ); ``` Flow-specific opening messages auto-injected on component init. **Flow IDs in use**: - Flow 3: Simple mode (text-only, no QA search) - Flow 6: Gemini File Search RAG (personal document Q&A, file upload enabled) - Flow 7: **學習規劃探索助手** (Learning Planning Exploration Assistant) — direct Gemini multi-turn conversation - Flow 8: **未來教室設備支援助理** (Classroom FAQ Assistant) — Gemini multi-turn + image attachment support ### 4. **Build & Deployment** **`package.json`** (lines 11-12): ```javascript "predeploy": "pnpm run build", "deploy": "gh-pages -d dist" ``` **Single SPA build model**: - `vite build` produces one main bundle (`dist/` folder) - Deployed to GitHub Pages as a static site - Built with **Vite** as the bundler **`vite.config.ts`** (lines 27-45): ```javascript build: { rollupOptions: { input: { main: path.resolve(__dirname, "index.html"), demo: path.resolve(__dirname, "demo/index.html"), embed: path.resolve(__dirname, "src/embed.ts"), }, output: { entryFileNames: (chunk) => { if (chunk.name === "embed") return "embed/bundle.min.js"; return "assets/[hash:10].js"; }, }, }, } ``` **Three entry points** (multi-entry build): 1. **`main`** (`index.html`): The main SPA (all flows together) 2. **`demo`** (`demo/index.html`): Standalone demo page showing the embed widget doesn't affect external page styling 3. **`embed`** (`src/embed.ts`): Web Component bundle (`embed/bundle.min.js`) for widget embedding in third-party sites **No code-splitting by flow**: The main build is one bundle containing all flows; flow selection at runtime is via route.query. ### 5. **Existing "Special Flow" Precedent (Flow 8)** Flow 8 (Classroom FAQ) already has **per-flow custom UI** implemented via **conditional rendering**, NOT separate routes or components: **In `src/components/InputBlock.vue` (line 125)**: ```vue ``` Conditional component (not a separate page). **`src/components/ImageAskInput.vue`**: A simple button component that: - Opens a file picker accepting only images - Stores the image in provider state (`attachedImage` ref) - Displays a thumbnail preview when image is selected (InputBlock lines 91-109) - Clears image after send (ChatProvider line 207) **In `src/hooks/ChatProvider.vue`**: - Lines 42-46: `attachedImage` state (persists across messages) - Lines 204-207: Appends image to user message display: `"${content}\n📎 已附加照片"` - Lines 375-376: Image passed to backend in `callAIWrapper`: `...(image ? { image } : {})` **Backend flow-specific handling** (`chatai_backend/Controllers/RunController.cs` lines 222-286): - Flow 8 has dedicated handler `RunClassroomFaqFlow()` that: - Extracts image from request body (lines 259-266) - IP whitelist check (line 224-232) - Passes image to `IClassroomFaqChatService.QueryStreamAsync()` (line 272) **Pattern used**: `v-if="route.query.flow === 'X'"` inline conditionals throughout components. There is **no separate Vue page/component for flow 8** — it's all one `MainPage.vue` with conditional UI blocks. ### 6. **Iframe/Web Component & Micro-Frontend Patterns** The app has **existing Web Component embedding capability** for third-party site integration: **`src/embed.ts`** (Web Component class `ShadowWidget`, line 67): ```javascript customElements.define("ntu-chatbot", ShadowWidget); ``` **Architecture**: - Defines custom element `` using Shadow DOM (`mode: "open"`) - Renders FAB (floating action button) and iframe - Iframe src points to the main app (line 23): `this.iframe.src = import.meta.resolve(import.meta.env.BASE_URL);` - **PostMessage bridge** (lines 33-42, 62-64) for cross-iframe communication: - Host → iframe: `resize` events (viewport width) - Iframe → host: `close` / `toggle-fullscreen` events **Deployment model**: - Main app distributed as one HTML + JS bundle (SPA) - Embed bundle (`embed/bundle.min.js`) is separate entry point, can be loaded standalone - **Backend serves static files** (`Program.cs` line 131-132): ```csharp app.UseDefaultFiles(); app.UseStaticFiles(); ``` — single static folder, no per-flow separation **No pre-existing multi-build or micro-frontend pattern for flows**: All flows share one code tree and one build. The embed.ts is for embedding *the entire app* as a widget, not for separating flows. ### 7. **Backend Flow Architecture** (`chatai_backend`) **`Controllers/RunController.cs`** (lines 66-124): Flow detection happens at **signature level** (from JWT or fingerprint), then routed: ```csharp var apiFlowIndex = _signatureContext.apiFlow; if (apiFlowIndex == GeminiFlowIndex) // 6 return await RunGeminiFlow(body); if (apiFlowIndex == AdvisingFlowIndex) // 7 return await RunAdvisingFlow(body); if (apiFlowIndex == ClassroomFaqFlowIndex) // 8 return await RunClassroomFaqFlow(body); // Fallback: proxy to external Langflow server for flows 0-5, 9+ var flowId = flowIds.Skip(apiFlowIndex).First(); var targetUrl = $"{apiUrl}/api/v1/run/{flowId}"; ``` **Dedicated services per flow**: - Flow 6: `IGeminiFileSearchService` (file search RAG) - Flow 7: `IAdvisingChatService` (multi-turn advising, supports model switching: gemini/openai/claude) - Flow 8: `IClassroomFaqChatService` (multi-turn with image, IP whitelist, account type awareness) All three return **SSE streams** (`text/event-stream`) with format: `data: {delta, source, done, error}\n\n`. --- ## Summary for Integration Planning **Current Architecture:** - Single SPA with one `/` route; all flows co-exist in one codebase - Flow identified via `route.query.flow` query parameter - Flow 6, 7, 8 have flow-specific backend services but **share the generic MainPage/InputBlock/Messages Vue components** - Per-flow UI customization is done via `v-if="route.query.flow === 'X'"` conditionals inline in shared components - Global styles applied at root level; no per-flow CSS isolation yet - Web Component embed capability exists but is for wrapping the entire app, not for separating flows **Constraints for Flow 7 Integration:** 1. Global HTML/body CSS resets from `index.css` and `tailwind.config.js` apply site-wide (no per-flow scope) 2. Single router instance; routing to flow 7 means injecting into the same `/` route with a query param 3. Flex layout at `#app` level may conflict with your separate app's `body { overflow: hidden }` if nested directly 4. `ChatProvider.vue` wraps the entire app; messages state is global 5. Header component is shared across all routes and flows 6. No existing pattern for lazy-loading or code-splitting per flow in this build **Design Options** (not in scope of this report, but the facts above inform them): - Option A: Add flow-7-specific component files (with their own CSS/router isolated in Shadow DOM) and render via `v-if="flow === 7"` in MainPage - Option B: Separate build entry point for flow 7, served at different base path (e.g., `/flow7/`), co-exist with main app - Option C: iframe or Web Component wrapping for flow 7 to isolate styling and routing fully --- **Key File Paths Summary:** - Routing: `src/main.ts` (line 27-48) - Root layout: `src/App.vue`, `src/Providers.vue` - Flow branching: `src/components/MainPage.vue`, `src/hooks/ChatProvider.vue` - Flow 8 precedent: `src/components/ImageAskInput.vue`, `src/components/InputBlock.vue` - Global styles: `src/assets/index.css`, `tailwind.config.js` - Build config: `vite.config.ts` - Embed/Web Component: `src/embed.ts` - Backend flow logic: `chatai_backend/Controllers/RunController.cs`, `chatai_backend/chatai.Core/Service/`
